verdict.rationale: Pipecat documents functions, via Pipecat Flows, that interface with external systems and APIs during a conversation, with metadata auto-derived from function signatures. It also suggests handing long-running tools off to subagents. Nothing in the evidence shows how results are spoken back or how dead air is avoided during tool calls. Missing for 10: documented handling of dead air during tool execution (filler speech, async or non-blocking calls), evidence of results being spoken back, core-pipeline function-calling docs beyond Flows, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, my agent can call external APIs and custom functions mid-conversation and speak the result without awkward dead air

citations.quote: Process data by interfacing with external systems and APIs
Flows auto-derives the function's metadata — name, description, parameter properties (with their descriptions), and which parameters are required — from the function's signature and docstring.
Hand off to subagents for long-running tools and complex tasks
